mainTopic: Helping others sin, business with idol worshippers before their festivals, and the משנה's list of forbidden loans and payments
overview: This amud opens with a ברייתא: you may not hand wine to a נזיר or אבר מן החי to בני נח, because of לפני עור. The גמרא explains that this is a case where the two stand on opposite sides of a river, so the sinner needs your help. Next, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about whether profits from forbidden business with idol worshippers before their festival are forbidden after the fact, and a ברייתא backs ריש לקיש. A story follows in which ריש לקיש advises רבי יהודה נשיאה to drop a festival-day coin into a pit so that it looks like an accident. The גמרא then asks why the משנה forbids borrowing and collecting from them, which seem to hurt them rather than help them. אביי calls these a protective rule, and רבא says every case may lead the idol worshipper to thank his idol. The גמרא shows why each case in the משנה had to be taught, and defends רבי יהודה's view that collecting debts is allowed. Last, רב הונא rules like רבי יהושע בן קרחה about loans made without a document, and like רבי יהודה in a case of a dyer. That case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא: no handing wine to a נזיר or אבר מן החי to בני נח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק of לפני עור that you may not hand a forbidden item to someone who is not allowed to have it.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that a person may not hand a cup of wine to a נזיר, or a limb from a living animal to a non-Jew? The פסוק says: 'Do not put a stumbling block before the blind.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that forbids handing someone an item he is not allowed to use. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the פסוק of לפני עור as more than tripping a blind man. It also means helping someone else do an עבירה. A נזיר may not drink wine, and בני נח may not eat אבר מן החי, so handing them these things is helping them sin.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who took a vow not to drink wine, among other restrictions
A limb cut from a living animal, forbidden even to non-Jews
Non-Jews, who must keep the seven Noahide laws
The prohibition of causing or helping another person to sin
'The verse teaches', which introduces a פסוק as the source

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the idea that helping another person sin is itself forbidden.

phrases.english: From where do we know that a person may not hand
a cup of wine to a nazirite,
or a limb from a living animal to descendants of Noah?
The verse teaches:
"And before the blind do not place a stumbling block";

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא יוֹשִׁיט אָדָם כּוֹס שֶׁל יַיִן לְנָזִיר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Handing a forbidden item to someone who may not use it violates לפני עור.

steps.title: But he could have taken it himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that in these cases the person could get the item on his own, yet the ברייתא still says the giver violates לפני עור.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, if we don't give it to him, he could take it himself, and still the giver transgresses לפני עור!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a difficulty from the ברייתא. The person could have taken the wine or the limb himself, so how is handing it to him 'putting a stumbling block' in his way?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual idea is that you only violate לפני עור if your help actually makes the sin possible. In the ברייתא's cases the sinner seems able to manage without you. If the ברייתא still forbids it, then even helping someone who could sin anyway would be forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָכָא, דְּכִי לָא יָהֲבִינַן לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: But here, where if we do not give it to him,
he can take it himself,
and yet the giver transgresses because of
"Before the blind do not place a stumbling block"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא, דְּכִי לָא יָהֲבִינַן לֵיהּ, שָׁקְלִי אִיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the ברייתא's cases fit the meaning of לפני עור
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that לפני עור applies only when the sinner could not manage without you
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A נזיר or non-Jew could normally take the item himself, yet the ברייתא still calls handing it לפני עור.

steps.title: They are standing on two sides of a river
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a case where the sinner could not reach the item without help.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where they are standing on two sides of a river.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about a special case. The item is on the other side of the river, so the sinner really could not get it without you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By placing the case across a river, the גמרא keeps the rule that לפני עור applies only when your help is truly needed. In this case the giver's help is what makes the sin possible.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What case are we dealing with here?', which narrows a source to a specific situation

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא is about a case where the sinner cannot reach the item without help, like across a river.

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?
Where they are standing on two sides of a river.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be about a sinner who could take the item himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about a sinner who cannot reach the item, so the giver's help is truly needed.

steps.title: The word 'hand across' supports the river case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's wording 'יושיט' (hand across or extend) rather than 'give' fits a case of reaching across a river.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is exact too. It says 'he may not hand across' and not 'he may not give.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer from the exact wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יושיט' means stretching something out to someone, which suits handing it across a river. If the ברייתא meant ordinary giving, it would have said 'יתן'. So the wording itself points to the river case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The wording is exact too', which brings support from precise language
'Learn from this', which confirms the point

phrases.english: The wording is exact too, since it teaches "he may not hand across"
and it does not teach "he may not give,"
learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 3
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא is about two sides of a river

steps.title: What if someone already did business before their festival?
steps.stepSummary: A question is raised: if someone ignored the משנה and did business, what is the status of his profits?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if someone did business, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. If someone did business with idolaters when the משנה said not to, are the profits forbidden after the fact?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids doing business beforehand, before the person acts. Now the question is what happens afterward. Must the earnings be treated as forbidden?

keyTerms.meaning: 'A question was asked before them', which opens a genuine question

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
If one did business, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means doing business with idolaters around their festival, which the משנה forbids. The question is about the profits.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether profits from forbidden business with idolaters are forbidden after the fact

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: forbidden. ריש לקיש: permitted
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים disagree about whether the profits are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: if he did business, the profits are forbidden. ריש לקיש says: if he did business, they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two opposite answers to the question. רבי יוחנן forbids the profits and ריש לקיש permits them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that the profits are forbidden even after the fact. ריש לקיש holds that the prohibition was only about not doing the business in the first place, so once it is done, the money is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי שמעון בן לקיש, רבי יוחנן's study partner

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: נָשָׂא וְנָתַן — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: if he did business, it is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: נָשָׂא וְנָתַן — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: Reish Lakish says: if he did business, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: נָשָׂא וְנָתַן אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two answers to the question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן: the profits are forbidden. ריש לקיש: the profits are permitted.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says profits from business on 'their festivals' are forbidden. רבי יוחנן suggests it means before their festivals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: 'On the festivals of idolaters, if one did business, the profits are forbidden.' Isn't this about before their festivals?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a ברייתא that says the profits are forbidden. He claims it is talking about our case, business done before the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'their festivals' in the ברייתא really means the days before the festival, then the ברייתא forbids exactly the profits that ריש לקיש permits.

keyTerms.meaning: Their festivals, meaning the idolaters' holidays
'Is it not...?', which suggests a reading of the source

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan challenged Reish Lakish:
On the festivals of idolaters,
if one did business, the profits are forbidden.
Is it not referring to before their festivals?

steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that the profits are permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read as 'before their festivals', the ברייתא forbids the profits of exactly the case under discussion.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the ברייתא means on the festival itself
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the ברייתא is about business done on the festival day itself, not before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means their festivals exactly.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש pushes back. The ברייתא is only about business on the festival day itself, which is a stricter case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Business on the festival itself is more severe, so its profits may be forbidden. That says nothing about the days before. So ריש לקיש's view still stands.

phrases.english: No, it means their festivals exactly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's challenge
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Their festivals' means only the festival day itself.

steps.title: Another version: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, ריש לקיש uses the same ברייתא against רבי יוחנן. It only forbids profits on the festival, which implies that before it they are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say ריש לקיש challenged רבי יוחנן: 'On the festivals of idolaters, if one did business, it is forbidden.' On their festivals, yes. Before their festivals, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the argument. Here it is ריש לקיש who quotes the ברייתא as a challenge to רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the ברייתא forbids profits only from business on the festival itself. That suggests profits from business before the festival are permitted, which goes against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes ... no, an inference from what the source includes and leaves out

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same ברייתא as in step 7, but now it is used for the opposite side. Read simply, it supports ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: Some say it went like this:

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish challenged Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: אֵידֵיהֶן שֶׁל גּוֹיִם — נָשָׂא וְנָתַן אָסוּר.
phrases.english: On the festivals of idolaters, if one did business, it is forbidden.
On their festivals, yes; before their festivals, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that the profits are forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids only festival-day business, which implies that profits from before the festival are permitted.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the תנא calls both 'their festivals'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the ברייתא uses the word 'their festivals' for both the festival and the days before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא calls both the days before and the festival itself 'their festivals.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defends himself. In the ברייתא, 'their festivals' covers the days before the festival too, so it does forbid those profits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the reverse of ריש לקיש's answer in the first version. There, 'their festivals' meant only the festival day. Here, it includes the days before. In both versions the argument comes down to how wide the word 'אידיהן' is.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן forbids profits from business before their festivals and ריש לקיש permits them. Each one reads 'אידיהן' in the ברייתא to fit his own view.

phrases.english: The תנא, both this and that,
calls "their festivals."
phrases.notes: In other words, the days before the festival are also included in the word 'their festivals.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא, אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי, אֵידֵיהֶן קָרֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's challenge in the second version
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Their festivals' means only the festival day.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Their festivals' includes the days before the festival as well.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא limits the ban on business to items that last. It also says that if someone already did business, even with lasting items, the profit is permitted. This matches ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with ריש לקיש: When the Sages said it is forbidden to do business with them, they only forbade items that last. Items that do not last are not forbidden. And even with items that last, if someone already did business with them, the profit is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports ריש לקיש in the argument about whether profits from this business are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban covers only items that last, since the idol worshipper could use them for his festival. The last line is the proof: even when someone broke the rule and traded lasting items, the profit is still permitted after the fact. That is ריש לקיש's position against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him
To do business (literally, to carry and to give)
An item that lasts (does not spoil quickly)

steps.whatToRemember: This ברייתא backs ריש לקיש. The ban is only on items that last, and even then, profits made after the fact are permitted.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Reish Lakish:
When they said, 'It is forbidden to do business with them,'
they only forbade it with an item that lasts,
but with an item that does not last, no.
And even with an item that lasts,
if he did do business, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings outside support for ריש לקיש after the back-and-forth over the first ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's view that profits from forbidden business are permitted after the fact
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: even with a lasting item, if one did business, it is permitted

steps.title: Non-lasting items: sell to them, but do not buy from them
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד teaches, from the school of רבי אושעיא, that items that do not last may be sold to them but not bought from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד taught from the school of רבי אושעיא: An item that does not last may be sold to them, but it may not be bought from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another teaching that refines the rule about items that do not last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last ברייתא made it sound as if items that do not last are fully allowed. This teaching allows only selling them. Buying from them is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: From the study hall (school) of רבי אושעיא

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַב זְבִיד בִּדְבֵי רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Rav Zevid taught from the school of Rabbi Oshaya:
An item that does not last, we may sell to them,
but we may not buy from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב זְבִיד בִּדְבֵי רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the permission for non-lasting items given in the previous ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Non-lasting items may be sold to idol worshippers before their festival but not bought from them.

steps.title: A coin gift on a festival day puts רבי יהודה נשיאה in a dilemma
steps.stepSummary: A מין sends רבי יהודה נשיאה a coin on his festival day. רבי יהודה נשיאה asks what to do. If he takes it, the man will thank his idol. If he refuses, the man will become his enemy.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain מין sent a Caesarean coin to רבי יהודה נשיאה on the day of the מין's own festival, while ריש לקיש was sitting before him. רבי יהודה נשיאה said: What should I do? If I take it, he will go and thank his idol. If I do not take it, he will hold a grudge against me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up a practical question. It prepares for ריש לקיש's advice in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two concerns pull against each other. Accepting the gift gives the giver a reason to thank his idol, and that is the worry behind the ban. Refusing it could create dangerous hatred.

keyTerms.meaning: A Caesarean dinar, a type of coin
He goes and gives thanks (to his idol)

phrases.english: There was a certain heretic who sent
a Caesarean dinar to Rabbi Yehuda Nesia
on the day of his festival.
Reish Lakish was sitting before him.
He said: What should I do?
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבי יהודה נשיאה, asking ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: If I take it, he will go and give thanks,
if I do not take it, he will have hatred.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מִינָאָה דְּשַׁדַּר לֵיהּ דִּינָרָא קֵיסָרְנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from rules about business to a real-life case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to handle a gift from an idol worshipper on his festival day without causing thanks to the idol or hatred

steps.title: ריש לקיש: take it and throw it into a pit
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש advises him to take the coin and throw it into a pit in front of the man.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: Take it and throw it into a pit in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers רבי יהודה נשיאה's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking the coin avoids insulting the man. Throwing it away means no benefit is gained from a festival-day gift.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to him:
Take it and throw it into a pit in front of him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Accept the coin, then throw it into a pit in front of the giver.

steps.title: That would cause even more hatred
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה נשיאה objects: throwing the gift away in front of the man will make him hate me even more.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: All the more so, he will hold a grudge!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה נשיאה pushes back on ריש לקיש's advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole point was to avoid hatred. Openly throwing the gift away is a bigger insult than refusing it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן דְּהָוְיָא לֵיהּ אֵיבָה!
phrases.english: He said: All the more so he will have hatred!
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבי יהודה נשיאה again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's advice.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's advice to throw the coin into a pit in front of the giver
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Openly throwing the gift away insults the giver even more than refusing it, so the hatred gets worse.

steps.title: Make it look like an accident
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that he meant to drop the coin in a way that looks accidental.
steps.simpleTranslation: I meant that you should do it in a backhanded way.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש clarifies his advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the coin seems to slip from his hand into the pit, the giver is not insulted. Yet no benefit is gained from the gift, so both concerns are handled.

keyTerms.meaning: In an unusual way, backhandedly (so it looks accidental)

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's solution handles both concerns: no benefit is gained from the festival gift, and no open insult causes hatred.

phrases.english: It is in a backhanded way that I was saying.
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש is speaking. He means: let it seem to fall from your hand by accident.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection by clarifying how to throw the coin.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Throw the coin away openly, which would insult the giver
steps.terutzMaskana: Drop it in a way that looks accidental, so there is no insult and no benefit

steps.title: Why is borrowing items from them forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids lending items to them and borrowing items from them. Lending makes sense because it helps them. But borrowing takes things away from them, so why forbid it?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'to lend items to them and to borrow items from them.' Lending to them makes sense, since it benefits them. But borrowing from them actually leaves them with less, so why is it forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and questions its second case, borrowing items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the ban is that we should not help idol worshippers before their festival. Lending fits that reason. Borrowing does the opposite, because it takes their things away during the festival, so the ban needs an explanation.

phrases.english: 'To lend items to them and to borrow items from them,' etc.
It makes sense to forbid lending to them, since it gives them gain,
but borrowing from them,
is it not actually reducing what they have?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and goes back to the next phrase in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ban on borrowing items from idol worshippers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ban exists so as not to help them, and borrowing takes from them instead of helping them.

steps.title: אביי: borrowing was forbidden so people would not come to lend
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the Sages forbade borrowing as a גזירה, so that people would not come to lend.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is a גזירה. Borrowing from them was forbidden because of lending to them.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question with a protective rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Borrowing itself is not the problem. The Sages forbade it so that people would not mix it up with lending, which really does help them.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective rule made by the Sages

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is a decree: borrowing from them was forbidden because of lending to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Borrowing should be allowed, since it does not help them
steps.terutzMaskana: Borrowing is forbidden to keep people away from lending

steps.title: רבא: both are forbidden because he will thank his idol
steps.stepSummary: רבא says lending and borrowing are both forbidden for one reason: the idol worshipper will go and thank his idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: All of it is forbidden because he will go and give thanks to his idol.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a different answer from אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the issue is not whether the idol worshipper gains. Any deal that pleases him, even a Jew needing to borrow from him, may lead him to thank his idol, so borrowing is forbidden directly.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי and רבא agree that borrowing is forbidden. They only disagree about why: אביי says it is a protective rule, and רבא says it is the same reason as lending.

phrases.english: Rava said:
All of it is because he goes and gives thanks.
phrases.notes: He is pleased that the Jew needed him, so he thanks his idol.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר כּוּלָּהּ מִשּׁוּם דְּאָזֵיל וּמוֹדֶה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same question, different from אביי's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the ban
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban is only about giving them gain
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban is about causing him to thank his idol, which applies to borrowing too

steps.title: Why is borrowing money from them forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The same question is asked about money. Lending money to them makes sense, but why forbid borrowing money from them?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'to lend money to them and to borrow money from them.' Lending to them makes sense, since it benefits them. But why is borrowing from them forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase in the משנה, which is about money, and asks the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the earlier question for loans of money instead of items. Borrowing money does not seem to help them, so the ban needs a reason.

phrases.english: 'To lend money to them and to borrow money from them.'

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְהַלְווֹתָם — מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא מַרְוַוח לְהוּ,
phrases.english: It makes sense to forbid lending to them, because it gives them gain,
but borrowing from them, why is it forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְהַלְווֹתָם מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא מַרְוַוח לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same question as step 17, now about money loans.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ban on borrowing money from idol worshippers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Borrowing money from them does not give them gain, so why forbid it?

steps.title: אביי: borrowing money was forbidden so people would not come to lend
steps.stepSummary: אביי again says it is a גזירה: borrowing money was forbidden because of lending money.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is a גזירה. Borrowing money from them was forbidden because of lending money to them.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the same kind of answer he gave for items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here too, borrowing is forbidden only to keep people away from lending money, which does help them.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is a decree: borrowing from them was forbidden because of lending to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about money.
steps.terutzMaskana: Borrowing money is forbidden to keep people away from lending

steps.title: רבא: both are forbidden because he will thank his idol
steps.stepSummary: רבא again says that both lending and borrowing money are forbidden because the idol worshipper will thank his idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: All of it is forbidden because he will go and give thanks to his idol.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the same answer he gave for items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is the same for money: any deal that pleases the idol worshipper before his festival may lead him to thank his idol.
steps.whatToRemember: For loans of items and loans of money alike, אביי forbids borrowing as a protective rule. רבא forbids both lending and borrowing because the idol worshipper will thank his idol.

phrases.english: Rava said:
All of it is because he goes and gives thanks.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר כּוּלָּהּ מִשּׁוּם דְּאָזֵיל וּמוֹדֶה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same question, different from אביי's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the ban
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban is only about giving them gain
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban is about causing thanks to the idol, which applies to borrowing money too

steps.title: Why is collecting a debt from them forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the last pair in the משנה and asks: paying them makes sense, but collecting from them reduces their money.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said it is forbidden to pay back debts owed to them and to collect payment from them. Paying them is understandable, because it gives them profit. But collecting from them takes money away from them, so why is it forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the last pair in the משנה's list and asks the same kind of question it asked before. One side of the pair makes sense, but the other side seems to hurt the עובד עבודה זרה rather than help him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying a debt to him puts money in his hand, so he may feel blessed and thank his idol. Collecting a debt from him does the opposite and lowers his wealth. So why would the משנה forbid it?

keyTerms.meaning: To pay them back (repay a debt owed to them)

steps.confusionAlert: Careful: לְפוֹרְעָן means the Jew pays THEM, and לִפְרוֹעַ מֵהֶן means the Jew collects FROM them. The words look alike but point in opposite directions.

phrases.english: To repay them and to collect payment from them, etc.
Granted, repaying them is forbidden,
because it gives them a profit.
But collecting payment from them:
doesn't that reduce their money?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְפוֹרְעָן מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא מַרְוַוח לְהוּ, אֶלָּא לִפְרוֹעַ מֵהֶן מַעוֹטֵי מְמַעֵט לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same question pattern from Steps 17 and 20 to the last pair in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ban on collecting debts from them.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason is to avoid giving them profit, collecting a debt takes profit away, so it should be allowed.

steps.title: אביי: Collecting was forbidden because of repaying
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that collecting debts was forbidden as a גזירה so people would not come to repay debts.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The Sages forbade collecting from them as a protective rule, because of repaying them.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the same kind of answer he gave for the earlier pairs. Collecting is not a problem by itself, but the Sages forbade it to protect against repaying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, only repaying actually brings the problem of profit. Collecting was added as a fence so that people would not mix up the two and end up repaying before the festival.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of; out of concern for

phrases.english: אביי said: Collecting from them is forbidden as a decree
because of repaying them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23 with אביי's consistent approach, as in Steps 18 and 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Collecting from them has no real problem since it lowers their money.
steps.terutzMaskana: Collecting is forbidden only as a fence around the real ban on repaying.

steps.title: רבא: Both are forbidden because he will thank his idol
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both repaying and collecting are forbidden for one reason: he will go and thank his idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: All of it is forbidden because he will go and give thanks to his idol.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his same answer as before. Every case in this pair is forbidden directly, for one shared reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, even when the עובד עבודה זרה pays a debt, he may thank his idol that he had enough money to pay. So collecting is a real problem by itself, not just a fence.

keyTerms.meaning: He goes and gives thanks (to his idol)

steps.whatToRemember: For every pair in the משנה: אביי says the second half is a גזירה because of the first half, and רבא says both halves are forbidden because he will go and thank his idol.

phrases.english: רבא said:
All of it is because he goes and gives thanks.
phrases.notes: He means thanking his idol, the same worry רבא raised in Steps 19 and 22.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: כּוּלָּהּ מִשּׁוּם דְּאָזֵיל וּמוֹדֶה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to Step 23's question, parallel to Steps 19 and 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Single shared reason for both cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Collecting from them should be allowed because it lowers their money.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even paying a debt can lead him to thank his idol, so collecting is forbidden on its own.

steps.title: Why the משנה needed both business and borrowing items
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins showing that every case in the משנה is needed: from business alone, we would have allowed borrowing items.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the cases are needed. If the משנה had taught only business with them, we would say that is forbidden because it gives him profit and he will thank his idol. But borrowing items from them reduces what he has, so it would be fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why the משנה listed so many cases instead of just one. This is the first of three links in the chain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Business clearly helps him, so it is forbidden. Borrowing an item from him takes it away from him for a while, so we might have allowed it. That is why the משנה had to say it outright.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed; all the cases had to be taught
To borrow an object (to be given back)
It is fine; it is allowed

steps.confusionAlert: Two different kinds of borrowing appear here. לִשְׁאוֹל means borrowing an item you return as it is, while לִלְווֹת (in the next step) means borrowing money you pay back.

phrases.english: And they are all needed.
For if it had taught only doing business with them,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא מַרְוַוח לְהוּ וְאָזֵיל וּמוֹדֶה,
phrases.english: that is because it gives them profit, and he goes and gives thanks.
But borrowing items from them,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמַעוֹטֵי קָא מְמַעֵט לְהוּ — שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: which reduces what they have, would be fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the questions on each pair, the גמרא steps back to explain why the משנה lists all the cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Borrowing items could not be learned from business, since borrowing reduces his property.

steps.title: Why the משנה needed both borrowing items and borrowing money
steps.stepSummary: From borrowing items alone, we would have allowed borrowing money, because lending money only worries him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught only borrowing items from them, we would say that is forbidden because it feels important to him, and he goes and thanks his idol. But borrowing money from them only causes him worry, since he says: 'My money will not come back again.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second link in the chain. The גמרא shows that borrowing money could not be learned from borrowing items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a Jew needs to borrow an item, the עובד עבודה זרה feels important and pleased, so he thanks his idol. Lending money makes him nervous that he will lose it, so we might think there is no thanking and it would be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter feels important to him

phrases.english: And if it had taught only borrowing items from them,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דַּחֲשִׁיבָא לֵיהּ מִילְּתָא, וְאָזֵיל וּמוֹדֶה.
phrases.english: that is because the matter feels important to him, and he goes and gives thanks.
But borrowing money from them,
he only has worry from it,
since he says: 'The money will not come back again.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the צריכותא from borrowing items to borrowing money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Borrowing money could not be learned from borrowing items, since lending money brings him worry, not pride.

steps.title: Why the משנה needed collecting debts too, so every case is needed
steps.stepSummary: From borrowing money alone, we would have allowed collecting from them, since paying back only upsets him. So every case had to be taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught only borrowing money from them, we would say that is forbidden because he says: 'I will collect it from him even against his will,' so for now he goes and gives thanks. But collecting from them, where the money will not come back to him, you might say he is upset and does not go and give thanks. So it is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last link in the chain, and then the גמרא concludes that every case in the משנה had to be taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he lends money, he feels safe because he can force repayment with the loan document, so he still thanks his idol. When he has to pay his debt, the money is gone for good and he is upset. So without the משנה saying it, we would have allowed collecting from him.
steps.whatToRemember: Each case in the משנה teaches something new. Business, borrowing items, borrowing money, and collecting debts each have a reason we might have allowed it, so the משנה had to forbid each one by name.

phrases.english: And if it had taught only borrowing money from them,
that is because he says: 'I will collect from him against his will,'
and for now, at least, he goes and gives thanks.
But collecting payment from them,
where the money will not come back to him again,

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא צַעֲרָא אִית לֵיהּ, וְלָא אָזֵיל וּמוֹדֶה
phrases.english: I might say he is upset and does not go and give thanks.
So it is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the צריכותא chain begun in Step 26 and closes it with צְרִיכָא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: No case in the משנה's list can be learned from another, so each had to be stated on its own.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה ignore later happiness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה from the משנה and asks whether he rejects the idea that someone upset now may be happy later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says we may collect debts from them. Does רבי יהודה not accept that even if the borrower is upset now, he will be happy later?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's view in the משנה and starts a challenge against it. The proof for the challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה allows collecting debts because paying back only upsets the גוי, so he will not thank his idol. The גמרא asks: a person who pays off a debt may feel relieved and happy afterward. Doesn't רבי יהודה care about that later happiness?

keyTerms.meaning: collecting a debt that is owed to you

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One may collect debts from them, etc.
And does Rabbi Yehuda not hold
'even though he is upset now,
he is happy later'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from showing that every case in the משנה is needed to examining רבי יהודה's dissenting view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's reasoning that collecting is allowed because the גוי is only upset
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If later happiness counts, paying a debt could lead to happiness and then thanks to the idol, so collecting should be forbidden.

steps.title: The lime case shows רבי יהודה counts later happiness
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה allows a woman to apply removable lime on חול המועד because she will be happy afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה says a woman may not apply lime on חול המועד, because it makes her look bad. But he agrees that lime she can peel off during the מועד she may apply during the מועד. Even though she is upset now, she will be happy later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove its challenge. In it, רבי יהודה himself uses the reasoning 'upset now, happy later.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lime makes the skin look ugly at first, but once it is peeled off the woman looks better. רבי יהודה allows it when it comes off during the מועד, because her later happiness counts. So he does accept 'happy later', and this seems to clash with his ruling about debts.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the middle days of the festival

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
A woman may not apply lime during the festival days,
because it makes her look ugly.
And Rabbi Yehuda agrees about lime
that she can peel off during the festival days,
that she may apply it during the festival days,
since even though she is upset now,
she is happy later!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source that powers the challenge raised in step 29.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה accepts the idea 'upset now, happy later'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a woman applying lime on חול המועד

steps.title: The laws of מועד are a special case
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that חול המועד laws are different, because all its permitted work is based on 'upset now, happy later.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Leave aside the laws of חול המועד. In all of them, a person is upset now but happy later.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the challenge by saying the lime case cannot be compared to debts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On חול המועד, the whole idea of the permitted work is that the effort is hard now but brings joy on the festival. So 'happy later' is built into those laws. That does not mean רבי יהודה uses this reasoning everywhere, such as with a גוי paying a debt.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Leave aside the laws of the festival days,
because in all of them, he is upset now
and (she is) [he is] happy later.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out 'she' in round brackets; the corrected word in square brackets is 'he', since this is about everyone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised from the lime ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the laws of מועד are unique
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה always counts later happiness, so he should forbid collecting debts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Counting later happiness belongs to the special rules of חול המועד. It does not apply to debts.

steps.title: A גוי is always upset about paying back
steps.stepSummary: רבינא gives a different answer: רבי יהודה does count later happiness, but a גוי paying a debt is never happy about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: A גוי, when it comes to paying back a debt, is always upset.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a second answer to the same challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא agrees that רבי יהודה normally counts later happiness. He says it simply does not apply here, because a גוי stays upset about paying a debt even afterward. So there is no later happiness that could lead him to thank his idol.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
A non-Jew, when it comes to paying back,
is always upset.

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers for רבי יהודה: רב נחמן בר יצחק says 'happy later' is special to חול המועד laws. רבינא says a גוי never becomes happy about paying a debt.
steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: גּוֹי לְעִנְיַן פֵּרָעוֹן לְעוֹלָם מֵיצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the same challenge that רב נחמן בר יצחק answered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction about the case itself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Paying off a debt brings later relief and happiness.
steps.terutzMaskana: For a גוי, paying back is always upsetting, so the principle never applies here.

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow רבי יהושע בן קרחה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה does not follow רבי יהושע בן קרחה, who allows collecting a loan made without a document because the money might otherwise be lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like רבי יהושע בן קרחה. It was taught: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says that a loan with a document may not be collected from them, but a loan made by word of mouth may be collected from them, because he is like someone saving his money from their hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a new point: our משנה forbids collecting debts without making any split, so it does not follow רבי יהושע בן קרחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a document, the lender can collect later, so he should wait until after the festival. Without a document, he may never get paid, so collecting now is like rescuing his money, and רבי יהושע בן קרחה allows it. Our משנה makes no such split.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה does not follow (the view of)
a loan written in a document
a loan made by word of mouth, with no document
like someone rescuing his money from them

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע בן קרחה does not argue about the reason of upset versus happy. His split is about whether the lender risks losing his money.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה,
phrases.english: Our Mishnah is not like Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it was taught: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says:
A loan with a document, one may not collect from them,
a loan by word of mouth, one may collect from them,
because he is like one saving his money from their hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יהודה discussion and identifies a תנא whose view our משנה does not follow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה forbids collecting all debts before their festivals. רבי יהושע בן קרחה allows collecting a loan made without a document, because of the risk of losing the money.

steps.title: רב הונא rules like two תנאים
steps.stepSummary: While his students sat before him, רב הונא stated that the הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה and also follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף sat behind רבי אבא, and רבי אבא sat before רב הונא. רב הונא sat and said: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה, and the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about רב הונא teaching his students. He gives two practical rulings without explaining them yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא said our משנה does not follow רבי יהושע בן קרחה. Now רב הונא says the practical הלכה does follow him. His second ruling, about רבי יהודה, is stated without a case, so the גמרא will need to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: before him, the way a student sits before his teacher

steps.whyThisMatters: This tells us how to rule in practice. The הלכה here follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה, not the plain reading of the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב יוֹסֵף אֲחוֹרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef sat behind Rabbi Abba,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָתֵיב רַבִּי אַבָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Abba sat before Rav Huna,
phrases.notes: Sitting before someone means learning from him as his student.

phrases.english: and he sat and said:
phrases.notes: The one speaking is רב הונא, the teacher.

phrases.english: The halakha follows Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha,
and the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיָתֵיב וְקָאָמַר: הִלְכְתָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling on the opinion of רבי יהושע בן קרחה that was just mentioned in step 33, and adds a second ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה and also follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Which ruling of רבי יהושע בן קרחה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ruling like רבי יהושע בן קרחה refers to the case just discussed, collecting a loan made without a document.
steps.simpleTranslation: The halakha follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה: this refers to what we just said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining רב הונא's two rulings. It says the first one is about the case we already learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן קרחה allowed collecting a loan made without a document from a גוי before his holiday, because otherwise the money might be lost. רב הונא rules that this is the practical הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: that which we said; something already mentioned

phrases.english: The halakha follows Rabbi Yehoshua:
this is what we said,
phrases.notes: This points back to the loan made without a document, from step 33.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of רב הונא's two rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may collect a loan made without a document from a גוי before his holiday, following רבי יהושע בן קרחה.

steps.title: Which ruling of רבי יהודה: the dyer case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ruling like רבי יהודה refers to a teaching about a dyer who dyed wool the wrong color. The case continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: The halakha follows רבי יהודה, as it was taught: If someone gives wool to a dyer to dye it red for him, and the dyer dyed it black, or he asked for black and the dyer dyed it red...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the second ruling. It begins quoting the case about a dyer who used the wrong color, and the ruling itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a completely new topic, about damages and paying workers. It has nothing to do with idolatry. So far we only have the facts: the dyer went against his instructions. רבי יהודה's view on how he gets paid will follow.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the opinion of רבי יהודה from our משנה, about a גוי repaying a debt. רב הונא is pointing to a different opinion of רבי יהודה, in the dyer case.

phrases.english: The halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda:
as it is taught:
phrases.notes: This case appears in בבא קמא 100b.

phrases.english: One who gives wool to a dyer
to dye it red for him
and he dyed it black,
or asked for black and he dyed it red.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the second of רב הונא's two rulings, by pointing to a different source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of a dyer who did not follow his instructions. The ruling comes in the next section.
